# Fitting components

These captures are normal Go `/fits`, `/fit/PublicFit00001` and catalogue fragment
responses. A local in-process HTTP stub supplied one named Rifter, doctrine,
community fit and rating. No database or production writes ran. The temporary
capture test was removed. Tests mount the actual Go scopes/actions; the saved-fit
JSON seed is retained while executable shell/editor scripts are removed.

`render-source.json` contains output captured from the four original pure Go
browser JavaScript helpers in the private pre-TypeScript archive, using the
pinned dogma-engine/SDE 13.6.0 Rifter and boundary inputs from
`fitRenderParity.test.ts`. Expected output came from the original implementations,
not the TypeScript ports. The temporary VM/tar capture code was removed. Normal
tests load these committed-size fixture results and need no private archive.
They also assert meaningful wheel slots, charge icons, resource limits, EWAR,
expansion, drone controls and suggestion/observed-fit behavior.

`editor.html` is the normal Go `/fits/create` response with its actual component
scope and forms. The temporary capture test was removed. Editor controller tests
use the pinned SDE/Rust engine through a filesystem adapter and controlled local
HTTP/clipboard promises, without database writes or production dependencies.

`variants.html` is the real Go variants fragment from the opt-in local
`-reference-fittings -entity-database` comparison facade. It uses the existing
guarded read-only database for Rifter metadata and one explicitly named in-memory
family, including Go's zero-valued absent charges. No rows are inserted. Editor
tests load this markup to exercise observed preview, modified-preview reset and
restoring the retained custom workspace with the pinned engine.

`saved-editor.html` is the current Go `/fit/PublicFit00001` page from the same
local comparison facade, with its public Vexor and actual disposable API seed.
Unlike the creator, saved details omit the shortcut-help overlay. The combined
editor test proves initialization still renders the gun/charge, three active and
two stored drones, cargo quantity and calculated stats. No new save was submitted
to obtain this capture.
